:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y=4 \\ x+2y=16\end{aligned}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. It doesn't matter which equation we pick first, so we choose the easiest one. In this case, the first equation looks like the easiest.

Using the first equation, we can isolate $x$ by adding $y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y & =4 \\ x & =4+y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we replace $x$ with $4+y$ in the second equation and solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	x+2y &=16 \
	(4+y) + 2y &=16\
	4+3y &=16\
	3y &=12\
	y &=4
}
$$

If we now substitute $y=4$ into $x=4+y$, then we can find the value of $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	x &= 4 + y \
	   &= 4 + (4) \
	   &=8
}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x = 8$ and $y = 4$, which can be written as $(8, 4).$

$$
{\begin{aligned}b=480-10a \\ 20b+400a=7\,200\end{aligned}
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Notice that the first equation is already solved for $b:$

$$
b=480-10a
$$

So, we replace $b$ in the second equation and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}20b+400a & =7\,200 \\ 20(480-10a)+400a & =7\,200 \\ 9\,600-200a+400a & =7\,200 \\ 9\,600+200a & =7\,200 \\ 200a & =-2\,400 \\ a & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $a=-12$ into $b=480-10a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =480-10(-12) \\ b & =600\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-12,\,b=600.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
The pastry shop's total cost and revenue per month (in dollars) from selling cakes can be modeled by the equations $y=1\,600+5n$ and $y=64+17n,$ respectively, where $n$ is the number of cakes sold. 

Solve the system below using the substitution method to find the exact number of cakes needed to break even and the revenue made.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=1\,600+5n \\ y=64+17n\end{aligned}
$$

The pastry shop breaks even when$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\,$cakes are produced. 

The revenue made when selling this number of cakes is$\,$
{{field-2}}
$\,$dollars.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Notice that $y$ is isolated in the first equation. Therefore, we can replace $y$ with $1\,600+5n$ in the second equation and solve for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =64+17n \\ 1\,600+5n & =64+17n \\ 1\,600+5n-64 & =64+17n-64 \\ 1\,536+5n & =17n \\ 1\,536+5n-5n & =17n-5n \\ 1\,536 & =12n \\ \frac{1\,536}{12} & =\frac{12n}{12} \\ 128 & =n \\ n & =128\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $n=128$ into $y=64+17n$, then we can find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y=64+17(128)=2\,240\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the solution to the system of equations is $n=128$ and $y=2\,240.$
Therefore, the pastry shop breaks even when $128$ units are produced, and the revenue made when selling this number of units is $$2\,240.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Mary wonders where and when they'd meet if Sam left home $3.8$ minutes earlier and walked with a speed of $50$ meters per minute. She finds that the distance $d$ from home they'd meet can be modeled using the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}d+60t=960 \\ d-50t=190.\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ is the time (in minutes) since Mary left the community park.

Mary and Sam would meet$\,$
{{field-1}}$\,$minutes after Mary left the community park.

Mary and Sam would meet at a distance of $\,$
{{field-2}}$\,$meters from home.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To solve the given system of linear equations, we will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. It doesn't matter which equation we pick first, so we choose the easiest one. In this case, the second equation looks like the easiest.

Using the second equation, we can isolate $d$ adding to both sides of the equation $50t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d-50t=190 \\ d=190+50t\end{aligned}
$$

So, we replace $d$ with $190+50t$ in the first equation and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d+60t=960 \\ (190+50t)+60t & =960 \\ 190+110t & =960 \\ 110t & =960-190 \\ 110t & =770 \\ t & =\frac{770}{110} \\ t & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, they would have met after $t=7$ minutes.

If we substitute $t=7$ into $d=190+50t$, we can find the value of $d:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =190+50t \\  & =190+50(7) \\  & =540\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, they meet at a distance of $540$ meters from home.

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a - b$?

$\{3a-3b=-18; -2a+b=7$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2a+b & =7 \\ b & =7+2a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=7+2a$ into the first equation and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3a-3b & =-18 \\ 3a-3(7+2a) & =-18 \\ 3a-21-6a & =-18 \\ -3a-21 & =-18 \\ -3a & =3 \\ a & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $a=-1$ into $b=7+2a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =7+2(-1) \\ b & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a-b=-1-(5)=-6.$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Notice that the second equation is already solved for $y:$

$$
y=x-3
$$

So, we replace $y$ in the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5y & =21 \\ x+5(x-3) & =21 \\ x+5x-15 & =21 \\ 6x-15 & =21 \\ 6x & =36 \\ x & =6\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $x=6$ into $y=x-3,$ we can then find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(6)-3 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a - b$?

$\{-3a-2b=2; -3a+b=8$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3a+b & =8 \\ b & =8+3a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=8+3a$ into the first equation and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3a-2b & =2 \\ -3a-2(8+3a) & =2 \\ -3a-16-6a & =2 \\ -9a-16 & =2 \\ -9a & =18 \\ a & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $a=-2$ into $b=8+3a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =8+3(-2) \\ b & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a-b=-2-(2)=-4.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to this system using the method of substitution.

$\{3x+3y=2; 3x+y=-5$

The solution is $($ {{field-1}} $, $ {{field-2}} $)$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+y & =-5 \\ y & =-5-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=-5-3x$ into the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+3y & =2 \\ 3x+3(-5-3x) & =2 \\ 3x-15-9x & =2 \\ -6x-15 & =2 \\ -6x & =17 \\ x & =-\frac{17}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $x=-\frac{17}{6}$ into $y=-5-3x,$ we can then find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5-3(-\frac{17}{6}) \\ y & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-\frac{17}{6},\,y=\frac{7}{2}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to this system using the method of substitution.

$\{-3x+4y=8; -2x+y=6$

The solution is $($ {{field-1}} $, $ {{field-2}} $)$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+y & =6 \\ y & =6+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=6+2x$ into the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+4y & =8 \\ -3x+4(6+2x) & =8 \\ -3x+24+8x & =8 \\ 5x+24 & =8 \\ 5x & =-16 \\ x & =-\frac{16}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $x=-\frac{16}{5}$ into $y=6+2x,$ we can then find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =6+2(-\frac{16}{5}) \\ y & =-\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-\frac{16}{5},\,y=-\frac{2}{5}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a - b$?

$\{-5a+2b=9; -3a+b=3$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3a+b & =3 \\ b & =3+3a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=3+3a$ into the first equation and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5a+2b & =9 \\ -5a+2(3+3a) & =9 \\ -5a+6+6a & =9 \\ a+6 & =9 \\ a & =3 \\ a & =3\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $a=3$ into $b=3+3a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =3+3(3) \\ b & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a-b=3-(12)=-9.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $p - q$?

$\{4p=-24; p+5q=19$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the first equation, we can isolate $p$ by dividing both sides by $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4p & =-24 \\ p & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $p=-6$ into the second equation and solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p+5q & =19 \\ (-6)+5q & =19 \\ 5q & =25 \\ q & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p-q=-6-(5)=-11.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a - b$?

$\{-3a-3b=6; -4a+b=-7$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4a+b & =-7 \\ b & =-7+4a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=-7+4a$ into the first equation and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3a-3b & =6 \\ -3a-3(-7+4a) & =6 \\ -3a+21-12a & =6 \\ -15a+21 & =6 \\ -15a & =-15 \\ a & =1\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $a=1$ into $b=-7+4a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =-7+4(1) \\ b & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a-b=1-(-3)=4.$

Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a - b$?

$\{-2a-4b=-14; -2a+b=6$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2a+b & =6 \\ b & =6+2a\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}-2a-4b & =-14 \\ -2a-4(6+2a) & =-14 \\ -2a-24-8a & =-14 \\ -10a-24 & =-14 \\ -10a & =10 \\ a & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $a=-1$ into $b=6+2a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to this system using the method of substitution.

$\{5x-2y=5; 2x+y=-1$

The solution is $($ {{field-1}} $, $ {{field-2}} $)$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y & =-1 \\ y & =-1-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=-1-2x$ into the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-2y & =5 \\ 5x-2(-1-2x) & =5 \\ 5x+2+4x & =5 \\ 9x+2 & =5 \\ 9x & =3 \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $x=\frac{1}{3}$ into $y=-1-2x,$ we can then find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-1-2(\frac{1}{3}) \\ y & =-\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=\frac{1}{3},\,y=-\frac{5}{3}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x,y)$ to this system using the method of substitution.

$\{2x+2y=12; -2x+y=5$

The solution is $($ {{field-1}} $, $ {{field-2}} $)$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the second equation, we can isolate $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+y & =5 \\ y & =5+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=5+2x$ into the first equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+2y & =12 \\ 2x+2(5+2x) & =12 \\ 2x+10+4x & =12 \\ 6x+10 & =12 \\ 6x & =2 \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $x=\frac{1}{3}$ into $y=5+2x,$ we can then find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =5+2(\frac{1}{3}) \\ y & =\frac{17}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=\frac{1}{3},\,y=\frac{17}{3}.$
